introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.
enonce_intro_markdown: The following formulae represent some members of two homologous series: $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is a homologous series?

(ii) Identify the two series:

$\mathrm{C_2H_4}$: ................ $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$: ................ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds with the **same general formula and the same functional group**, so they have similar chemical properties; each member differs from the next by a $\mathrm{CH_2}$ unit, and the physical properties change gradually along the series.

(ii) $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ (ethene) belongs to the **alkenes**, general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$. $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$ (ethane) belongs to the **alkanes**, general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select from the list a compound that undergoes addition reaction with chlorine.

Compound: ................

Equation: ................ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Only the unsaturated compound (it has a $\mathrm{C=C}$ double bond) adds on chlorine. Compound: **$\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ (ethene)**.

Equation: $\mathrm{C_2H_4} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_4Cl_2}$ (1,2-dichloroethane, $\mathrm{CH_2Cl{-}CH_2Cl}$)

questions.enonce_markdown: Briefly describe how $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ can be distinguished from $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bubble each gas through **bromine water** (or shake with it).

- $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ (unsaturated) **decolourises** the orange-brown bromine water quickly.
- $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$ (saturated) causes **no change**: the bromine water stays orange-brown.

(Acidified potassium permanganate, decolourised by ethene only, also works.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Compound $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ can be converted to $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$.

(i) Identify the reagent used.

(ii) State the reaction condition. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The reagent is **hydrogen**: $\mathrm{C_2H_4} + \mathrm{H_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_6}$ (hydrogenation, an addition reaction).

(ii) Condition: a **nickel catalyst** at about **150 $^\circ$C** (finely divided nickel, moderate heating).

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one large scale use of $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any one of: manufacture of **poly(ethene) (polythene)** plastics by polymerisation; manufacture of **ethanol**; ripening of fruits.
